nodes.name: Lemma 2.22
Proposition 2.9: Prop
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $A_{11},\ldots,A_{\nu\nu}$ are all non-resonant, $d\in\mathbb{R}$ does not coincide with the anti-Stokes arguments of system (2.1), then we have
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align}
  
    \mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i} M_d}
    & = 
    (S^-_d)^{- 1} \cdot \mathrm{e}^{2 \pi \mathrm{i}
    \delta_u A} \cdot S^+_d, \\
    
    S^{\pm}_{d + 2 k \pi}
    & = 
    \mathrm{e}^{- 2 k \pi \mathrm{i} \delta_u
    A} \cdot S^{\pm}_d \cdot \mathrm{e}^{2 k \pi \mathrm{i} \delta_u
    A}, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z},\\
    
    S^{\pm}_{d \mp \pi} 
    & = 
    (S^{\mp}_d)^{- 1},\\
    
    S_d^\pm(c u+c_0I,\ensuremath{\operatorname{Ad}}(D)A+c_1I) & =
    \ensuremath{\operatorname{Ad}}(Dc^{\delta_uA})
    S_{d+\arg c}^\pm(u,A),\quad
    c\neq 0,
    \delta_uD=D,\\
    
    S_d^\pm(-u^\top,-A^\top) & =
    S_d^\pm(u,A)^{-\top}.
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
If we additionally assume that $A$ is non-resonant, then 
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align}

M_d
& = 
{C}_d \cdot A \cdot 
{C}_d^{- 1}, \\
{C}_{d + 2 k \pi}
& = 
\mathrm{e}^{-2k\pi\mathrm{i}\delta_u A} \cdot 
{C}_d\cdot
\mathrm{e}^{2k\pi\mathrm{i} A}, \quad k
\in \mathbb{Z}, \\

{C}_{d \pm \pi}
& = 
S^{\pm}_d\cdot {C}_d,\\
    
    C_d(c u+c_0I,\ensuremath{\operatorname{Ad}}(D)A+c_1I) & =
    Dc^{\delta_uA}\cdot
    C_{d+\arg c}(u,A)\cdot
    c^{-A}D^{-1},\quad
    c\neq 0,
    \delta_uD=D,\\
    
    C_d(-u^\top,-A^\top) & =
    C_d(u,A)^{-\top}.
\end{align}
\end{subequations}

nodes.name: Lemma 2.16
nodes.statement:
There exists a function $\ensuremath{\operatorname{hol}}(u_s-\xi)$
holomorphic at $\xi=u_s$ such that
on $\mathbb{C}^{\mathcal B}_d(u)$
    \begin{align}
    (\mathcal B_d {F}_d)(\xi)_{st} 
    & = (I+O(u_s-\xi))
    (u_s-\xi)^{-A_{ss}}(A_{ss}-I)!\cdot
    \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\pi\mathrm{i} A_{ss}} (S_d^+)_{st}-
	\mathrm{e}^{-\pi\mathrm{i} A_{ss}} (S_d^-)_{st}}{2\pi\mathrm{i}}\\
    & \quad
    +\ensuremath{\operatorname{hol}}(u_s-\xi),\quad \xi\to u_s.
    
    \end{align}

nodes.name: Proposition 2.4: Prop
Corollary 2.24
nodes.statement:
\begin{subequations}
Suppose that $A$, $\delta_u A$ are diagonalizable,

and fix the argument $\arg(u_t-u_s)=-\tau$.
If the following limit exists, 
and none of $u_1,\ldots,u_\nu$
lie inside the segment $[u_s,u_t]$ or 
the ray $[u_t,\infty\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\tau})$,
then we have
\begin{align}

\lim_{p\to\infty}
(u_t-u_s)^{A_{ss}}p^{-A_{ss}}\cdot
\frac{(u_t-u_s)^p}{(p-1)!}({H}_p^{[\infty]})_{st}\cdot
p^{A_{tt}}(u_t-u_s)^{-A_{tt}} & =
\frac{(S_{[\tau]})_{st}}{2\pi\mathrm{i}},


\\\lim_{p\to\infty}
(u_t-u_s)^{A_{tt}}p^{-A_{tt}}\cdot
({H}_p^{[s]})_{t\ast} \frac{p!}{(u_t-u_s)^p}\cdot
p^{A}(u_t-u_s)^{-A} & =
({C}_{\tau\pm\varepsilon})_{t\ast}.

\end{align}











\end{subequations}

nodes.name: Corollary 2.23
Proposition 2.20: Prop
nodes.statement:
For distinct $s,t\in\{1,\ldots,\nu\}$,
denote the path class with arguments $\boldsymbol\gamma_{st}^{(d)}$ 
as a path in $\mathbb{C}_d(u)$ from $u_s$ to $u_t$ 
with arguments
\begin{align}
    \theta_s \in 
    \left\{\begin{array}{ll}
     (-d-2\pi,-d), 
     & \ensuremath{\operatorname{Im}} (u_s \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} d}) > 
     \ensuremath{\operatorname{Im}} (u_t \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} d})\\
     (-d,-d+2\pi), 
     & \ensuremath{\operatorname{Im}} (u_s \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} d}) < 
     \ensuremath{\operatorname{Im}} (u_t \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} d})
    \end{array}\right.,\quad
    \theta_t \in (-d-\pi,-d+\pi),
\end{align}
and denote the path class with arguments 
$\boldsymbol\gamma_{s\infty}^{(d)} := 
([u_s,\infty\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} d}),-d,-d)$,
$\boldsymbol\gamma_{\infty t}^{(d)} := 
((\infty\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} d},u_t],-d,-d)$
as a ray (see Figure Fig:path)
, then we have
\begin{align}
    \mathcal S_{u,A}(\boldsymbol\gamma_{st}^{(d)})
    = (S_d)_{st},\quad
    \mathcal S_{u,A}(\boldsymbol\gamma_{s\infty}^{(d)})
    = ({C}_d)_{s\ast} \cdot
    (\mathrm{e}^{\pi\mathrm{i} A} - \mathrm{e}^{-\pi\mathrm{i} A}),\quad
    \mathcal S_{u,A}(\boldsymbol\gamma_{\infty t}^{(d)})
    = (\mathrm{e}^{\pi\mathrm{i} A} - \mathrm{e}^{-\pi\mathrm{i} A})\cdot
    ({C}_d^{-1})_{\ast t}.
\end{align}
Denote the path class with arguments 
($\boldsymbol{e}_s^{l}$) $\boldsymbol{e}_s^r$
as a simple loop
starting from $u_s$ 
in a (counter-) clockwise direction
with arguments $\theta_s=\theta_t$
(see Figure Fig:path), 
then we have
\begin{align}
    \mathcal S_{u,A}(\boldsymbol{e}_s^{l}) 
    = \mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i} A_{ss}} - I,\quad
    \mathcal S_{u,A}(\boldsymbol{e}_s^{r})
    = I - \mathrm{e}^{-2\pi\mathrm{i} A_{ss}},\quad
    A_{\infty\infty}:= A.
\end{align}
}

nodes.name: Theorem 4.5
nodes.statement:
[Xu2]
For any $h\notin\mathbb{Q}$ and distinct $u_1,...,u_\nu$, 
consider the quantum confluent hypergeometric equation (1.1) associated to a representation $V$. Assume that the direction $d\notin \ensuremath{\operatorname{aS}}(u)$ is such that
    \begin{equation*}
      \ensuremath{\operatorname{Im}} (u_{1} \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} d}) >
      \ensuremath{\operatorname{Im}} (u_{2} \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} d}) > \cdots > 
      \ensuremath{\operatorname{Im}} (u_{\nu}  \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} d}),
    \end{equation*} then the (modified) Stokes matrices 
$L_{\pm} = q^{\mp \delta_u \mathbf{E}} 
S_d^{\pm} (u, - \hbar \mathbf{E})\in {\rm End}(V)\otimes{\rm End}(\mathbb{C}^\nu)$, of the quantum confluent hypergeometric equation (1.1) associated to a representation $V$, satisfy
\begin{equation}
R^{12}L_\pm^{(1)}L_\pm^{(2)}=L_\pm^{(2)}L_\pm^{(1)} R^{12},
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
R^{12}L_+^{(1)}L_-^{(2)} =L^{(2)}_{+}L^{(1)}_{-}(u) R^{12}.
\end{equation}
Here the convention is that if we write
$L_{\pm}=\sum_{i,j}(L_\pm)_{ij}\otimes E_{ij}\in {\rm End}(V)\otimes {\rm End}(\mathbb{C}^\nu)$,
then 
\[
L_{\pm}^{(1)}:= \sum_{i,j}(L_\pm)_{ij}\otimes E_{ij}\otimes I,\quad
L_\pm^{(2)}:= \sum_{i,j}(L_\pm)_{ij}\otimes I\otimes E_{ij},\quad
\text{and } R^{12}:=I\otimes R
\] 
as elements in ${\rm End}(V)\otimes  {\rm End}(\mathbb{C}^\nu)\otimes {\rm End}(\mathbb{C}^\nu)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2
Proposition 1.5: Prop
Proposition 3.1: Prop
Proposition 4.9: Prop
nodes.statement:
Suppose that the representative element $\tilde{\gamma}_{s_2t_2}$
    of path class with arguments is not self-intersecting, 
    particularly with $s_2\neq t_2$.
    
    Under the morphsim 
    $\mathfrak{S}(u_1,\ldots,u_\nu)
    \xrightarrow{\pi}
    U_q(\mathfrak{gl}_\nu)$ 
    induced by Theorem 4.4 and
    Theorem 4.5, 
    we have
    \begin{align}
        \pi(\tilde{\gamma}_{s_1t_1} \wedge
        \tilde{\gamma}_{s_2t_2}) =
        \frac{ 
        q^{-t( \tilde{\gamma}_{s_1t_1}, \tilde{\gamma}_{s_2t_2} )}
        \pi( \tilde{\gamma}_{s_1t_1} )
        \pi( \tilde{\gamma}_{s_2t_2} ) -
        q^{s( \tilde{\gamma}_{s_1t_1}, \tilde{\gamma}_{s_2t_2} )}
        \pi( \tilde{\gamma}_{s_2t_2} )
        \pi( \tilde{\gamma}_{s_1t_1} )}
        {q-q^{-1} },
    \end{align}
    where 
    $| \theta_s^{(2)} - \theta_s^{(1)} |,
     | \theta_t^{(2)} - \theta_s^{(1)} |,
     | \theta_t^{(2)} - \theta_t^{(1)} |,
     | \theta_s^{(2)} - \theta_t^{(1)} | < \pi$, and
    \begin{align}
        s( \tilde{\gamma}_{s_1t_1}, \tilde{\gamma}_{s_2t_2} ) & :=
        \delta_{s_1s_2} \ensuremath{\operatorname{sgn}}(\theta_s^{(2)} - \theta_s^{(1)}) -
        \delta_{s_1t_2} \ensuremath{\operatorname{sgn}}(\theta_t^{(2)} - \theta_s^{(1)}),\\
        t( \tilde{\gamma}_{s_1t_1}, \tilde{\gamma}_{s_2t_2} ) & :=
        \delta_{t_1t_2} \ensuremath{\operatorname{sgn}}(\theta_t^{(2)} - \theta_t^{(1)}) -
        \delta_{t_1s_2} \ensuremath{\operatorname{sgn}}(\theta_s^{(2)} - \theta_t^{(1)}).
    \end{align}
